owner_posts.post_text:
Post-Menopausal Bleeding: A Symptom That Should Never Be Ignored
A post-menopausal woman recently visited our clinic with vaginal bleeding. Since bleeding after menopause is never considered normal, we performed an ultrasound scan, which revealed a thickened endometrium (the lining of the uterus). To identify the cause accurately, a hysteroscopy was advised.
Hysteroscopy is a simple procedure that allows direct visualization of the uterine cavity using a small camera. During the procedure, we discovered a large endometrial polyp arising from the uterine lining. The polyp was removed completely and sent for laboratory testing.
Any bleeding occurring after 12 months of menopause should be investigated, even if it is only a few drops or happens just once. Common causes include polyps, endometrial thickening, hormonal changes, infections, and occasionally uterine cancer.
The good news is that early diagnosis with ultrasound and hysteroscopy allows timely treatment and excellent outcomes in most cases.
The key message: Never ignore post-menopausal bleeding. What appears to be a minor symptom may be your body's way of asking for attention. Early evaluation can lead to early diagnosis, effective treatment, and peace of mind.
At Momma's Clinic, we believe awareness and timely care are the first steps toward better women's health. 🌸

What is a Cervical Polyp? (Simple Explanation)
A cervical polyp is a small, soft growth that appears on the mouth of the uterus (cervix) — the opening between the uterus and the vagina.
👉 Think of it like a tiny skin tag or grape-like growth hanging from the cervix.
👉 Most of the time, it is harmless (non-cancerous).
Why does it happen?
We don’t always know the exact cause, but it may be linked to:
Hormonal changes (especially estrogen)
Chronic inflammation of the cervix
Increased blood vessel growth in the area
What symptoms can it cause?
Many women have no symptoms and it’s found during a routine check-up.
If symptoms occur, they may include:
Bleeding after intercourse
Irregular spotting between periods
White or yellow discharge
Occasionally, heavier periods
Is it dangerous?
In most cases, NO
Very rarely, it can be pre-cancerous or cancerous, which is why doctors usually:
Remove it
Send it for testing (biopsy)
How is it treated?
Hysteroscopy with polypectomy.
When should you see a doctor?
Consult a gynecologist if you have:
Bleeding after sex
Unusual discharge
Irregular bleeding
Or if a polyp was found during examination.
